answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid on jobs. Deleting an account cannot release the bond early; its record remains as a relic of the commitment. This turns an oasis of cheap usernames into a capital constraint: a delta of 1,000 active fake identities requires another $100,000 locked up. The attacker can still buy scale, but creating names alone buys no access.
